messages:
mike: Heads-up — spike in response-contract rejections on /v2/actions in eu-west. Rejections jumped from ~4% to ~12% over the past 2h. Most fail reason: "expected object, got array".

deploy-bot: [alert] 1732467960: contract-errors:euwest bucket threshold crossed (rule: response-contract-mismatch).

sarah: Do we have a rollout or client change around 2h ago? Any canary toggles?

anna: Mobile SDK v1.9.0 shipped ~2.1h ago to beta users — they changed attachments -> arrays in one codepath. Could be it.

mike: Good catch. It explains the array vs object. Two problems: (1) strict validation is rejecting and routing to degen path, (2) quota and billing attribution now counts these as failures which bloats error stats and affects SLA triggers.

tim: Right — and routing fallback is currently disabled for this contract (we reverted permissive behavior last month). That means customers see a hard reject instead of graceful coercion. Quota is still consumed when we hit the degen route.

leo: Quick suggestion: enable a short-lived permissive canary for this contract in eu-west to let adapter coerce arrays->object; at the same time mark these items with an audit tag so billing doesn't treat them as customer errors.

anna: We can implement an adapter shim to detect [attachments] array and convert to { attachments: ... } upstream. Patch would be 10–20 LOC. I can PR this now and gate behind a rollout flag.

sarah: We also need dashboard telemetry: add a panel that splits response-contract rejects by client-version and by country. Right now the error page only shows counts by model/route.

mike: Agreed. Action items:
- anna: PR adapter shim + canary flag (patch + test).
- leo: flip permissive-canary in eu-west for 1h after deploy, capture sample payloads.
- tim: update billing policy to treat these specific audit-tagged rejects as non-billable for the next 6h.
- sarah: add dashboard panel and a breakdown widget for client_version / route.

anna: PR opened -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/inference/commit/abc123 (draft). Includes unit tests and an opt-in flag `actions.contract_coerce_arrays`.

leo: Can we add a small sampling hook to capture the raw payloads (redact PII) so we can confirm transform correctness?

mike: Yes — sample 1% of these failures and store to long-term S3/secure bucket with retention 90d. Make sure logs include the audit tag `contract_coerce_candidate` and original client_version.

tim: Note on quota: if we treat them as non-billable, we need a temporary tag in billing pipeline and a migration to backfill counts for last 2h. I can coordinate with finance for the short window.

anna: Rolling out shim to canary in 15m. Will post updates here.

sarah: Dashboard card requested: `Actions / Response contract rejects by client_version` with a quick filter for eu-west. Ping me when metrics emitted. :thumbsup:

mike: If the canary stabilizes, we'll keep permissive for 24h and then reassess. If new SDKs keep sending arrays, we should ship coercion permanently or update SDK.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary(actions-contract-shim) -> eu-west at 1732468055 by anna.

anna: Deployed to canary. Observability: initial rejects dropped by ~80% in the sample slice. Will leave canary on for 1h and then expand if stable.

leo: Sampling hook collected 42 raw payloads so far. All look like same pattern. Redacting then uploading now.

mike: Thanks team. Follow-ups: make an SDK bug report to mobile team, and create postmortem note if billing backfill required. Closing here once billing tag applied.
